title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
why_read: A carefully constructed benchmark testing LLM reasoning over real wearable health data, useful for those building or evaluating health AI applications.
analysis: WearableQA is a benchmark of ~4000 multiple-choice questions built from real wearable sensor data across 200 users, designed to test whether LLMs can reason about longitudinal physiological signals rather than just pattern-match. The paper's dual-grounding methodology (combining literature-based physiology with statistically validated population patterns) is a thoughtful approach to benchmark construction, and the wide performance spread across 14 models (19.6%-72.9%) indicates the task has real discriminative power. This matters for engineers building health-AI copilots who need to know current LLM limitations in this domain.
